pairs.difference: A: the red cooler sits in the left-centre at a 3/4 angle. Its open lid nearly touches the top-left edge and it fills the card like the real reference. B: a flat, wide paddling pool fills the full width but only half the height. The duck, which should be the focal point, is a small shape in the upper middle. The fence takes up the whole top strip, and grass fills the bottom third with nothing in it.
pairs.fix: Bring the camera closer and lower so the paddling pool fills the card from top to bottom and is cropped by the side edges. Make the rubber duck large and in front, near the centre. Show only a sliver of fence at the top.

pairs.difference: A: the envelope is tilted on the boards and sits centred with even wood showing on all sides. The wax seal is a clear focal point. B: the book fills more of the card than any real card does (subject area 0.53). Its spine and ribbons run almost to the right edge. Five stickers compete across the cover, so no single feature reads first.
pairs.fix: Pull the book back so even wood shows on all four sides. Put one large sticker on the cover instead of several small ones.

pairs.difference: A: the parasol is small and floats in the upper middle with wide empty rings around it (subject area 0.175, below the real range). The thin handle hangs into empty space. B: the beach umbrella's canopy spans nearly the full width and is tilted, so it reads at a glance.
pairs.fix: Draw the parasol much larger and tilted, with its canopy spanning almost the full card width. Leave the hooked handle reaching down toward the bottom-right corner.

pairs.difference: A: the two gloves lie in a diagonal pair from the top-right to the bottom-left, like the real flippers card, and fill the card. B: the fan is an open semicircle seen nearly face-on, in the upper middle. The yellow background is empty below and around it, and the fan's flat outline reads like a sticker.
pairs.fix: Turn the fan to a 3/4 angle and tilt it so it fills the card diagonally. Bring the handle closer to the viewer and lower the fan so it sits in the middle of the card.

pairs.difference: A: the armchair is placed squarely in the centre with even margins all round (margin 0.117, above the real range). It is a static frontal block. B: the rocking chair is at a 3/4 angle, its finials nearly touch the top-right corner, and its rockers run across the floor.
pairs.fix: Bring the armchair closer at a 3/4 angle so its wing back nearly touches the top edge and one armrest is near the side edge. Show less empty floor in front of it.

pairs.difference: A: the jacket sits at a 3/4 angle with the sleeves spreading near both side edges. The sash cuts across it diagonally and gives a clear first read. B: the top hat is centred and level against a plain radial burst, with nothing to anchor it. It looks symmetric and floats in the middle like the generated lesson cards.
pairs.fix: Tilt the top hat to a jaunty 3/4 angle, with its brim dipping toward the bottom-left. Make it larger so its crown is close to the top edge.

pairs.difference: A: the inkwell is small at the bottom left, and the feather rises in a thin diagonal. The card is mostly empty stripes and table (subject area 0.21, width 0.65, both below the real range). B: the fountain spreads across the full width and is cropped by its plaza, like the real barrel card.
pairs.fix: Bring the inkwell and quill much closer and make them larger. The bottle should fill the lower half and the feather should sweep up to the top-right corner.

pairs.difference: A: the ship's wheel fills the card face-on, with its handles reaching close to the edges. It reads at once. B: the gramophone is narrow (width 0.49, below the real range). The horn sits in the upper left and the box sits low, which leaves an empty purple band on the right and a wide band of empty floor below.
pairs.fix: Bring the gramophone closer at a 3/4 angle so the horn and box together fill the card's width. Let the horn's rim nearly touch the top-left edge.

pairs.difference: A: the spotlight hangs from a truss that is cropped by the top edge, and its beam runs off the bottom-left corner. This edge cropping matches the real cards. B: the coral clump is centred on a flat green floor with even margins all round. Several branches compete equally and no single shape leads.
pairs.fix: Bring the coral closer so its tallest branch nearly touches the top edge. Make one big branch dominant in front and crop the rocks at the bottom edge.

pairs.difference: A: the ring box sits tilted at a 3/4 angle, with its open lid near the top. The gold coin is the clear focal point. B: the pocket watch's face is seen flat-on, and its chain reaches off to the right as a second focus. The flat face reads as a 2D clock rather than an object.
pairs.fix: Turn the pocket watch to a 3/4 angle so its rim shows depth. Curl the chain down below the watch instead of to the side, and make the watch larger in the card.

pairs.difference: A: the door is a narrow strip in the middle of a wide brick wall (width 0.505, below the real range). Pink flower clusters in the top corners and potted bushes in the bottom corners compete for attention. B: the door is cropped close by the card edges, and the wreath at the centre reads at once.
pairs.fix: Bring the camera close so the green door and its fanlight fill most of the card, with the frame cropped by the side edges. Remove the flower clusters from the corners.

pairs.difference: A: the vending machine stands tall and fills most of the card's height, with a clear upright read. B: the teacup and saucer are short and wide in the lower middle (height 0.47, below the real range, and margin 0.14, above it). The upper half is empty purple with only faint steam.
pairs.fix: Bring the teacup closer and view it from a little higher, so the cup and saucer fill the card from near the top to near the bottom edge.

pattern: Generated cards show the whole object placed politely in the centre. They are often seen face-on or level, with even margins and leftover empty background. Real cards push the object close to or past an edge at a 3/4 tilt and give it a single dominant shape. Generated cards also tend to let extra parts compete with the hero: corner foliage, a side chain, scattered stickers or a clump of equal shapes.
